title: DCC RPG Dying Earth - thoughts during an unboxing
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9BmwbWSPXwY

Daniel (@dungeondive) unboxes Goodman Games' Dungeon Crawl Classics Dying Earth box sets and reaches a verdict he clearly didn't want to reach. He states his position up front: he's not a fan of DCC as a system — weak starting characters, too many modifiers, rules that get in the way — but he loves the books as source material, and he loves Jack Vance.

The Vance digression is the warmest stretch of the video. He walks his shelf, complains about every Dying Earth cover ever printed, and pays real tribute to Gollancz's Fantasy Masterworks line for bringing decades of out-of-print fantasy back within reach in the early 2000s. He places Dying Earth closer to Gene Wolfe's Book of the New Sun than to Conan, and notes how directly Vance's memorised, named spells shaped D&D magic — comparing it to kung fu masters calling out attacks and counters.

Then the boxes. The Player's Librum leans hard into Vancian magic and verbiage, with a glossary, spell lists and a d100 magician quirks table; he flags d100 unusual landmarks and the bestiary as genuinely useful to a soloist. The stretch goal box offers dungeons, a hex crawl, a judge's screen and art folios. His honest conclusion: the art is superb, the focus is magic not place, and he'll likely pass it on.

----

Daniel buys books from systems he doesn't play, purely to mine the tables and lore. Which game's books earn shelf space in your house despite never hitting your table?
